Implementation

The method is tool-agnostic. But there is an open implementation.

You can apply KDV with documents, with the platform you already have, or with the reference implementation: a predominantly open-source data lakehouse, installed as code and verified with every change.

KDV modules

One interface for each role.

Modules organise the work by who uses them; accountability stays with the roles.

Share · Activate

KDV Consumer

Those who find and use data. Catalogue, time-limited access requests, contract reading and tracking of grants.

Cultivate · Govern · Share

KDV Producer

Those who prepare and publish data. Domains, subdomains, contracts, versions, quality and decisions on access requests.

Govern

KDV EcOps

Those who govern the ecosystem. Common policies, governance profiles, roles, forum decisions and indicators.

Shared foundation

KDV PlatOps

Those who operate the platform. Environments, services, alerts, certificates and secrets, without showing their values.

Activate

KDV Desk

Everyone. Common desk for questions, problems and data incidents.

Shared foundation

Adapters

Platform engineering. Connect the model to the chosen tools, without separate product versions.

Licences and alternatives

Open by choice, with an explicit policy.

The stack is predominantly open source, with a documented licence policy and a software bill of materials (SBOM) generated with every build.

No lock-in to a single supplier

Each component has its version, licence and conditions of use recorded. The target is any conformant Kubernetes; platform differences live in the Adapters, not in separate product versions.

Other tools work too

The model does not require this stack. Organisations already using, for example, Airflow for orchestration, dbt Core for transformation or OpenLineage for lineage apply the same accountability model. The list above describes the reference implementation; alternatives are options to evaluate in your context.
